title: Energy levels & spectra
examples: What is the relationship between energy and wavelength?
How do atoms give off light?
Can you explain what an energy level is?

explain.say: When electrons move in an atom, they jump between specific energy levels. These levels are like rungs on a ladder.
When an electron moves from a higher energy level to a lower one, it releases energy. This released energy is a photon.
This process of releasing a photon is called emission. The photon carries the exact energy difference between the levels.
Conversely, when an atom absorbs a photon, an electron jumps to a higher, or excited, energy level. This is absorption.
The change from one level to another is called a transition. The energy of the photon tells us about the energy gap.
In everyday life, neon signs glow with specific colors because the gas atoms are only allowed to emit photons of certain energies.

faq.q: Why are the energy levels discrete, not continuous?
faq.a: Electrons can only exist at specific, fixed energy levels within an atom. They cannot have any energy in between these allowed levels.
asks: Why can't electrons have any energy?
Are the energy jumps always the same size?

faq.q: What determines the color of the light emitted?
faq.a: The color depends on the energy difference, or the transition, between the two energy levels. Different gaps mean different photon energies and thus different colors.
asks: How does the energy gap relate to color?
Does the atom decide the color?

faq.q: Is absorption the opposite of emission?
faq.a: Yes, they are opposites. Emission happens when energy is released as a photon, and absorption happens when the atom takes in a photon.
asks: If I absorb energy, what happens next?

faq.q: Does the type of atom change the energy levels?
faq.a: Yes, every element has a unique set of electron energy levels because the number of protons in the nucleus is different.
asks: Do different elements have different spectra?
Does the nucleus affect the energy?

faq.a: A photon is a quantum of electromagnetic energy, which is a particle of light. It carries energy proportional to its frequency.
asks: Is a photon a particle or a wave?

facts: Electrons exist in discrete, quantized energy levels within an atom.
Emission occurs when an electron drops from a higher to a lower energy level.
Absorption occurs when an electron gains energy by absorbing a photon.
The energy of the emitted or absorbed photon equals the difference in energy levels ($\Delta E$).
The energy of a photon is related to its frequency by $E = hf$.

quiz.say: An electron moves from an energy level of three units to one unit. The energy of the emitted photon is:
quiz.why: The energy released is the difference between the starting and ending energy levels.

wrong.0: This only considers the final, lower energy level.
wrong.2: You cannot square the energy difference unless the question specifies it.
wrong.3: This is the sum of the levels, not the difference.

quiz.say: If an atom absorbs a blue photon, the electron moves to:
quiz.why: Absorption always causes an electron to move to a state with more energy.

wrong.0: The atom must absorb energy to move up to a higher state.
wrong.2: The ground state is the lowest possible energy level.
wrong.3: Lower levels are reached by emission, not absorption.

quiz.say: When an atom emits light, the resulting spectrum shows:

options.show: A continuous rainbow of all colors
options.say: A continuous rainbow of all colors

quiz.why: Because energy transitions are quantized, only specific amounts of energy (colors) can be emitted.

wrong.1: A continuous spectrum implies energy can be emitted in any amount, which is not true for atoms.
wrong.2: Atoms can emit energy across the entire electromagnetic spectrum, not just visible light.
wrong.3: The emission process itself creates the light, so the background is usually visible.
